     PRIME Search — task 1.8 SearchBench sources fetch

     Context

     data/searchbench/searchbench_v0.jsonl ships 30 questions whose answer keys
     are drafts written
     from the author's knowledge, every one marked validated_by: null. docs/08
     §1 is blunt about
     why that is not good enough: coverage policy moved in 2023 (CGM) and
     2024–2026 (GLP-1), the
     author's knowledge is a snapshot, and the assignment is graded in September
     2026. Keys are data
     with provenance, not remembered facts.

     Task 1.8 builds step 2 of docs/08 §2: pull the current text of every
     governing document through
     the primitives, store it, and report where the live sources disagree with
     the draft. The human
     validation pass (step 3) is task 2.1, which is yours to run — this task
     produces its input.

     We already know one answer the diff must surface: the draft keys assert 
     "April 16, 2023" six
     times, and 1.3 measured L33822 as being on R16, 2024-10-01. docs/08 §2 says
     finding that
     is the point — "the pipeline caught policy drift the author did not know
     about" is a line for the
     technical statement.

     Two facts that shape the work, from reading the seed file:

     - 19 CGM records hang off two documents (L33822, A52464) that the records
       already carry
       URLs for. Trivial to resolve.
     - 11 records — every GLP-1 one plus cross-002 — name their governing
       documents only in prose:
       "CMS March 2024 Part D guidance on anti-obesity medications", "FDA Wegovy
       label",
       "CMS/HHS 2025 announcements", "SSA 1927(d)(2)(A)". These have no URL
       anywhere in the dataset
       and must be resolved by search.

     Approach

     eval/searchbench/fetch_sources.py, run as uv run --env-file .env python -m 
     eval.searchbench.fetch_sources. It never writes to the .jsonl — correcting
     keys is 2.1's job,
     and a script that edited the thing it is auditing would destroy the
     provenance trail.

     1. Load and validate the dataset

     eval/searchbench/schema.py — Pydantic models for docs/05 §1's record
     (BenchRecord,
     AnswerKey, RequiredClaim, RequiredEvidence, ForbiddenClaim), plus
     load_records().

     These live under eval/, not prime_search/schemas.py. CLAUDE.md ties
     schemas.py to
     docs/02, and docs/02 contains no bench record — docs/05 §1 defines it, and
     prime_search/
     should not grow an eval-side dependency. Loading 30 records through a
     validator now also means
     2.2's evaluators and 2.6's runner get a typed dataset for free.

     2. Resolve each governing document to a URL

     Three methods, tried in order, and which one was used is recorded:

     1. record_url — a URL in the same record's answer_key.sources whose text
        matches the id.
     2. id — L33822 / A52464 map to their CMS MCD URLs by pattern.
     3. search — primitives.tavily.search(descriptor, 
        include_domains=sources.PRIMARY_DOMAINS),
        top hit. PRIMARY_DOMAINS already exists and is exactly docs/08 §2's
        "cms.gov, MAC domains,
        fda.gov".

     A prose descriptor resolved by search is a guess, and the output says so:
     the index records the
     query, the URL, the tier and a needs_review flag for anything not resolved
     by id or record URL.
     "CMS/HHS 2025 announcements" will not resolve cleanly and the report must
     say that plainly rather
     than present whatever Tavily returned as the governing document.

     One data change: add ssa.gov to the sources.py tier table as 
     primary_policy. Two records
     name SSA 1927(d)(2)(A), the statute text lives on ssa.gov/OP_Home/ssact/,
     and the host is
     absent from the table — so the restricted search cannot reach it.
     sources.py's own docstring
     sanctions this: "a wrong guess is a one-line fix plus a test row, not a
     code change".

     3. Fetch and store

     primitives.tavily.fetch(url, docs=..., run_dir=...) — the same path the
     sub-agent uses, so tier
     refinement, date extraction and the raw-content fallback all apply. Written
     to
     data/searchbench/sources/:

     - <slug>.txt — document text, unmodified, so within.load_paragraphs offsets
       stay valid
     - index.json — per document: url, retrieved_at, revision_date,
       effective_date, tier,
       publisher, paragraph count, the resolution method above, and which record
       ids depend on it

     Metadata goes in index.json rather than a header in the .txt precisely so
     the text stays byte-
     identical to what BM25 and any future verbatim check will read. docs/08 §2
     step 4 commits this
     folder ("small text files with public-domain government content") so the
     report is reproducible.

     4. Highlight passages for the human pass

     For each record, for each required_claim and each
     required_evidence.key_phrases entry, run
     primitives.within.search_within over the governing document and keep the
     top passages. Written to
     data/searchbench/review/<record_id>.md: the question, the draft key, and
     under each claim the
     passages that bear on it — which is precisely what docs/08 §2 step 3 says
     the author reads.

     30 records × several passages is unreadable on a console, so the worksheets
     are files and the
     console gets the drift summary.

     5. The drift report

     Printed, and written to reports/searchbench-drift.md (matching
     reports/model-selection.md from
     the model-selection side quest). Four checks per record:

     ┌─────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     │    Check    │                           Flags                           │
     ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │             │ a date asserted in the draft key vs the document's actual │
     │ Dates       │  revision_date — docs/08 §2's own example, "L33822        │
     │             │ revision date found: … — draft expected 2023-04-16"       │
     ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │             │ each required_evidence.key_phrases entry that does not    │
     │ Key phrases │ appear in the fetched text; a phrase the evaluator will   │
     │             │ look for that the document does not contain is a broken   │
     │             │ key                                                       │
     ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Forbidden   │ a forbidden_claims entry whose wording still appears in   │
     │ claims      │ the live document — the draft says it was removed; if it  │
     │             │ is still there the draft is wrong                         │
     ├─────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Resolution  │ documents resolved only by search, or not at all          │
     └─────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

     Records are ranked by flag count, and the report leads with the six the
     dataset README already
     names as highest drift risk (glp1-path-005, chg-glp1-001, chg-glp1-003,
     chg-cgm-002,
     cgm-code-004, cgm-code-001) so 2.1 starts where the risk is.

      16 -                                                               
      17 -**Background**                                                 
      18 -                                                               
      19 -On April 2, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
         -(CMS) issued a final rule revising the Medicare Advantage (MA) 
         -Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program (Part D), a
         -nd Medicare Cost Plan Program. The Contract Year (CY) 2027 MA a
         -nd Part D final rule aims to improve quality and access to care
         - for people enrolled in these programs by finalizing updates to
         - MA and Part D Star Ratings quality measurements and streamlini
         -ng certain enrollment processes.                               
      20 -                                                               
      21 -**Updates to Star Ratings**                                    
      22 -                                                               
      23 -The Star Ratings system helps Medicare beneficiaries compare he
         -alth and drug plan quality. Star Ratings also determine Quality
         - Bonus Payments and impact rebates for MA contracts, currently 
         -rating MA-PD contracts on up to 43 measures, MA-only contracts 
         -on up to 33 measures, and Part D plans on up to 12 measures acr
         -oss five categories: outcomes, intermediate outcomes, process, 
         -patient experience, and access.                                
      24 -                                                               
      25 -CMS is finalizing two sets of major changes to the Part C and P
         -art D Star Ratings system. First, for the 2027 Star Ratings, CM
         -S is not implementing the Excellent Health Outcomes for All rew
         -ard (previously called the Health Equity Index reward) that was
         - developed to incentivize improved performance for a subset of 
         -enrollees and will continue the historical reward factor that e
         -ncourages consistently high performance for all enrollees acros
         -s all quality measures. Second, CMS is streamlining and refocus
         -ing the measure set by removing 11 measures focused on administ
         -rative processes and areas where beneficiaries cannot distingui
         -sh performance between plans due to high performance and little
         - variation. Additionally, CMS is adding a new Part C Depression
         - Screening and Follow-Up measure to address behavioral health g
         -aps starting with the 2027 measurement year and 2029 Star Ratin
         -gs. CMS is also finalizing a technical clarification from the C
         -Y 2026 MA and Part D proposed rule related to contract consolid
         -ations.                                                        
      26 -                                                               
      27 -These changes refocus the program on clinical care, outcomes, a
         -nd patient experience where meaningful performance differences 
         -exist across contracts and reduce administrative burden by remo
         -ving measures that provide little meaningful distinction betwee
         -n plans.                                                       
      28 -                                                               
      29 -**Implementing Certain Provisions of the Inflation Reduction Ac
         -t (IRA) of 2022**                                              
      30 -                                                               
      31 -The IRA of 2022 made major changes to the Medicare Part D presc
         -ription drug benefit and directed CMS to implement these change
         -s through 2026 via program instructions. With this program inst
         -ruction authority expiring, CMS is codifying these changes for 
         -2027 and beyond, including eliminating the coverage gap phase,

         - cost sharing for enrollees in the catastrophic phase, and inco

      11 +# Contract Year 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D Final Rule  
      12 +                                                               
      13 +Share                                                          
      14 +                                                               
      15 +**Contract Year 2027 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medica
         +re Advantage Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Progra
         +m, and Medicare Cost Plan Program (CMS-4208-F3/CMS-4212-F)**   
      16 +                                                               
      17 +**Background**                                                 
      18 +                                                               
      19 +On April 2, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
         +(CMS) issued a final rule revising the Medicare Advantage (MA) 
         +Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program (Part D), a
         +nd Medicare Cost Plan Program. The Contract Year (CY) 2027 MA a
         +nd Part D final rule aims to improve quality and access to care
         + for people enrolled in these programs by finalizing updates to
         + MA and Part D Star Ratings quality measurements and streamlini
         +ng certain enrollment processes.                               
      20 +                                                               
      21 +**Updates to Star Ratings**                                    
      22 +                                                               
      23 +The Star Ratings system helps Medicare beneficiaries compare he
         +alth and drug plan quality. Star Ratings also determine Quality
         + Bonus Payments and impact rebates for MA contracts, currently 
         +rating MA-PD contracts on up to 43 measures, MA-only contracts 
         +on up to 33 measures, and Part D plans on up to 12 measures acr
         +oss five categories: outcomes, intermediate outcomes, process, 
         +patient experience, and access.                                
      24 +                                                               
      25 +CMS is finalizing two sets of major changes to the Part C and P
         +art D Star Ratings system. First, for the 2027 Star Ratings, CM
         +S is not implementing the Excellent Health Outcomes for All rew
         +ard (previously called the Health Equity Index reward) that was
         + developed to incentivize improved performance for a subset of 
         +enrollees and will continue the historical reward factor that e
         +ncourages consistently high performance for all enrollees acros
         +s all quality measures. Second, CMS is streamlining and refocus
         +ing the measure set by removing 11 measures focused on administ
         +rative processes and areas where beneficiaries cannot distingui
         +sh performance between plans due to high performance and little
         + variation. Additionally, CMS is adding a new Part C Depression
         + Screening and Follow-Up measure to address behavioral health g
         +aps starting with the 2027 measurement year and 2029 Star Ratin
         +gs. CMS is also finalizing a technical clarification from the C
         +Y 2026 MA and Part D proposed rule related to contract consolid
         +ations.                                                        
      26 +                                                               
      27 +These changes refocus the program on clinical care, outcomes, a
         +nd patient experience where meaningful performance differences 
         +exist across contracts and reduce administrative burden by remo
         +ving measures that provide little meaningful distinction betwee
         +n plans.                                                       
      28 +                                                               
      29 +**Implementing Certain Provisions of the Inflation Reduction Ac
         +t (IRA) of 2022**                                              
      30 +                                                               
      31 +The IRA of 2022 made major changes to the Medicare Part D presc
         +ription drug benefit and directed CMS to implement these change
         +s through 2026 via program instructions. With this program inst
         +ruction authority expiring, CMS is codifying these changes for 
         +2027 and beyond, including eliminating the coverage gap phase, 
         +establishing a reduced annual out-of-pocket threshold, removing
         + cost sharing for enrollees in the catastrophic phase, and inco
         +rporating the Manufacturer Discount Program that replaced the C
         +overage Gap Discount Program on January 1, 2025. CMS is also co
         +difying additional operational changes including updates to Tru
         +e Out-Of-Pocket cost calculations, specialty-tier rules, reinsu
         +rance payment methodologies, and implementation of the Selected
         + Drug Subsidy.                                                 
      32 +                                                               
      33 +**Revise List of Non-Allowable Special Supplemental Benefits fo
         +r the Chronically Ill (SSBCI)**                                
      34 +                                                               
      35 +CMS is refining its regulations regarding cannabis products by 
         +amending current regulatory language to state more precisely th
         +at cannabis products that are illegal under applicable State or
         + Federal law, are not allowable as SSBCI. This clarification al
         +igns MA benefit policies with current federal law while maintai
         +ning safeguards.                                               
      36 +                                                               
      37 +**Provisions Related to Supplemental Benefits Being Finalized f
         +rom the CY 2026 Proposed Rule**                                
      38 +                                                               
      39 +CMS is finalizing two supplemental benefit policies that were p
         +roposed in the CY 2026 rule: (1) strengthening SSBCI administra
         +tion by clarifying eligibility requirements, and increasing tra
         +nsparency by requiring plans to publicly post their plan-develo
         +ped SSBCI eligibility criteria; and (2) codifying and clarifyin
         +g requirements for administering supplemental benefits through 
         +debit cards, including that debit cards be electronically linke
         +d to plan-covered items and services through a real-time identi
         +fication mechanism to verify eligibility of plan-covered benefi
         +ts (products) at the point of sale; and that debit cards be lim
         +ited to the specific plan year.

         + goals.                                                        
      18 +                                                               
      19 +Innovation Center Models are time-limited experiments that prov
         +ide a controlled environment to determine, through rigorous eva
         +luation, what approaches should be expanded nationwide, what sp
         +ecific components of an approach need further testing in succes
         +sor models and what approaches are not viable for expansion. As

         +e Center must be efficient and effective in its response.

         +d versus actual impact.

         +. Most models selected for early termination are within 2 years

     more" with quotes — silently disabling the check.
  3. The report said "38 flags across 30 records" because a defaultdict was
     mutated by its own sort key.

      290 +def _date_in_text(text: str, value: date) -> bool:            
      291 +    """Does the document itself mention this date, in any of t
          +he shapes CMS uses?"""                                        
      292 +    if not text:                                              
      293 +        return False                                          
      294 +    month = value.strftime("%B")                              
      295 +    candidates = (                                            
      296 +        value.isoformat(),                                    
      297 +        f"{value.month:02d}/{value.day:02d}/{value.year}",    
      298 +        f"{value.month}/{value.day}/{value.year}",            
      299 +        f"{month} {value.day}, {value.year}",                 
      300 +        f"{month} {value.day} {value.year}",                  
      301 +    )                                                         
      302 +    return any(candidate in text for candidate in candidates)

          +":                                                            
      313 +        return " [resolved by search - confirm the document be
          +fore acting]"                                                 
      314 +    return ""

      523 +def _in_removal_scope(prefix: str) -> bool:                   
      524 +    """Is the match governed by the nearest revision marker, a
          +nd is that a removal?                                         
      525 +                                                              
      526 +    CMS renders a whole revision row on one line: `Removed: ".
          +.." ... Added: "..."`.                                        
      527 +    Asking only whether "Removed" appears anywhere before the 
          +match meant text the same                                     
      528 +    row *added* was treated as retired — the mirror image of t
          +he bug this scoping                                           
      529 +    fixes. The nearest preceding marker wins, which is how the
          + row actually reads.                                          
      530 +    """                                                       
      531 +    markers = list(_REVISION_MARKER.finditer(prefix))         
      532 +    return bool(markers) and _REMOVAL_CONTEXT.fullmatch(marker
          +s[-1].group(1)) is not None                                   
      533 +                                                              
      534 +                                                              
      535 +# Every marker that opens a clause in a CMS revision row, not 
          +just the removing ones.                                       
      536 +_REVISION_MARKER = re.compile(

  The check docs/09 asks for is "run it; review the diff summary". 47 flags 
  across 23 of 30 records.

  The headline is exactly what docs/08 §2 predicted:
  - L33822 is on 2024-10-01, A52464 on 2025-02-18 — the drafts assert
    2023-04-16.
  - cgm-elig-002 requires "level 2"/"level 3" from L33822 — neither is in the 
    LCD; it defers the definition to A52464.
  - cgm-code-001 calls K0553/K0554 retired; they appear 19 and 16 times in the
    live article.
  - The Wegovy label uses MACE, not the spelled-out phrase the key requires.
  - 12 of 14 governing documents have no canonical id. Each search hit is marked
    a guess, not presented as the governing text.

  Beyond drift, two things the dataset itself gets wrong: six records break 
  docs/08 §4–§5 authoring rules, and oos-002's question embeds a synthetic 
  patient record — name, DOB, A1c — against CLAUDE.md's "not even synthetic". I
  flagged it mechanically but didn't edit the dataset; that's 2.1's.

  On the spec review — it was worth running. It found a class of bug I'd have
  shipped:

  Three of my checks would have actively corrupted keys during your validation
  pass. The worst: _resolution_for looked up evidence in the run-wide map, so
  glp1-path-001 was told "medically accepted indication" — the correct statutory
  term — was missing from a document it never names. And my date flag reported
  cgm-elig-001's claim "added by the revision effective April 16, 2023" as drift
  when it's correct — the 2023 row is still in the revision history. With three
  minutes per record you'd have overwritten a right answer. Both now say
  something different and true.

  It also caught that check_forbidden was silently inert for 9 of 10 real claims
  while the report's legend implied it had run — so cgm-code-001 printed "no
  drift detected" though its only real assertion was never tested. That's now
  reported as unchecked, and a new code check makes the comparison the README
  promised.

  And it caught me flagging oos-002's PHI while copying that string into two 
  newly committed files. Redacted now; verified no patient detail survives in
  any artifact.

  405 tests pass, lint clean, 24 decision-log lines. One deliberate narrowing: I
  kept ssa.gov out of PRIMARY_DOMAINS so a bench task doesn't silently widen
  every production search — fetch_sources asks for it explicitly instead.

  Two things still yours: the PRIME_MODELS__SUB → PRIME_MODELS__SUBAGENT typo in
  .env, and the judge/extractor/evaluator model decision before the Day 2
  bench. Next task is 2.1, which is a [G] gate and needs /validate-bench from
  you.
